## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
Two Important defects need fixing. The pull-request description breaks the AGENTS.md rule that requires a `## Testing` section. `slugify` also drops accented and other non-ASCII letters, which contradicts the "non-alphanumeric" behaviour the description promises. This review read the full diff, `app/slug.py`, `tests/test_slug.py` and `AGENTS.md`, and traced the regex in `app/slug.py:7` by hand; the tests were read, not run. Both new modules open with a docstring, as `AGENTS.md:3` requires.

## Changes
Adds `app/slug.py` with a `slugify(title)` helper. It lowercases the title, replaces each run of characters outside `[a-z0-9]` with a hyphen and trims hyphens from both ends. It also adds a parametrized test in `tests/test_slug.py`.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- PR body — correctness — Add a `## Testing` section to the PR description — The description has no `## Testing` section, which breaks `AGENTS.md:4`: "Every pull-request description has a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified." The body is one sentence describing the behaviour and never says how the change was verified. — Reviewers cannot tell from the description whether the new tests were run or how the change was checked, and the PR does not meet the project's contributor rules. — Fix: Add a `## Testing` section that says how the change was verified, for example which test command was run and its result.
- app/slug.py:7 — correctness — Non-ASCII letters are stripped instead of kept — With the title `"Café au lait"`, `slugify` returns `"caf-au-lait"`, and with `"日本語"` it returns `""`. The pattern `[^a-z0-9]+` treats every non-ASCII letter as a separator, but the PR description says the helper replaces "non-alphanumeric characters", and Python considers `é` and CJK characters alphanumeric. — Pages with accented titles get wrong URLs. Pages whose titles have no ASCII letters or digits all get the empty slug, so their URLs collide. — Fix: Decide on the intended behaviour. One option is to keep Unicode word characters with `re.sub(r"[\W_]+", "-", title.lower())`. Another is to transliterate first, for example with `unicodedata.normalize("NFKD", ...)` followed by dropping combining marks. Either way, update the description to match and add a test case with a non-ASCII title.
